scope: Architecture and systems that make existing RAM go further: CXL expanders/pooling/DDR4 reuse, tiered and persistent memory, LLM KV-cache tiering hardware, hardware memory compression, processing/compute-in-memory, HBM alternatives (LPDDR chiplets, HBF) and memory-fabric silicon. Hardware/system/IP only; pure software is left to branch D. Vendor-status claims tagged [UNVERIFIED-T] could not be re-opened this session (WebSearch budget exhausted, WebFetch DNS-blocked); primary evidence comes from public GitHub repos (Linux, vLLM, Dynamo, LMCache, Mooncake, SMDK, HMSDK, KTransformers, model configs) plus cross-referenced Phase-1 price sources.

cards.name: DDR4 Second-Life CXL Expander
cards.subbranch: CXL memory expansion / DIMM reuse (Microsoft-Meta style DDR4 recycling)
cards.what_it_is: A PCIe Gen5 x16 CXL 2.0 Type-3 add-in card or 1U 'JBOM' holding 8-12 decommissioned DDR4-3200 RDIMMs behind a merchant DDR4-capable CXL controller (Marvell Structera X 2404-class or Microchip SMC 2000-class). A U.S. EMS (e.g. Sanmina) assembles it, and it ships with burn-in and qualification to operators moving to DDR5-only Xeon 6 / EPYC 9005 servers. The process 'materials' are DRAM that is already fabbed and paid for, and the capital is DIMMs that are already depreciated.
cards.why_it_could_work: Hyperscalers reuse DDR4 behind CXL because reuse beats buying new DDR5. B's model gives the hyperscaler a +$2.0/GB advantage at the 2023 trough and +$13/GB in 4Q26, with the card at ~$0.49/GB and DDR4 dumped at ~50% of spot. Single-host Type-3 expansion is stabilizing in mainline Linux ([2]). Tiering is upstream (weighted interleave v6.9, DAMON migration v6.11). The added ~70-100 ns latency [UNVERIFIED-T, Pond] suits VM-density and in-memory DB capacity tiers.

cards.name: KV Pool Node (shared DRAM+CXL KV-cache appliance)
cards.subbranch: LLM inference KV-cache tiering - DRAM/CXL tier
cards.what_it_is: A 2U EPYC 9005 / Xeon 6 server (Supermicro or Dell OEM chassis) holding 3-6 TB of DDR5 plus E3.S CXL memory modules (Samsung CMM-D, Micron CZ122 or SK hynix CMM-DDR5), with 2x400G RDMA NICs. It ships with Mooncake Store / LMCache MP preconfigured to allocate KV on the CXL tier (/dev/dax). It is sold as a rack-shared 'KV memory node' that pools prefix and agent-session caches across GPU servers running vLLM/SGLang/Dynamo.
cards.why_it_could_work: KV is large: Llama-3.1-70B is 320 KiB/token at BF16 (40 GiB per 128k context); DeepSeek-V3 MLA is 68.6 KiB/token. Reloading a 128k context (20 GiB FP8) over 400G RDMA takes ~0.5 s, against ~41 s to recompute on one H100. Holding KV in DDR5 pays if a prefix is reused at least once every ~1.35 h at 4Q26 prices (~3.4 h in the glut). Mooncake reports 75% more requests within SLO at Kimi. vLLM requires the CPU tier as the staging tier, and LMCache/Mooncake already speak CXL /dev/dax.

evidence.title: Mooncake README + Mooncake Store deployment guide (Kimi serving platform)
evidence.shows: Opened. KV-cache-centric disaggregation lets Kimi handle 75% more requests within SLO. Store has CXL-aware allocation (--enable_cxl, /dev/dax, --allocation_strategy=cxl). Integrated into vLLM (May 2026) and TensorRT-LLM (Oct 2026).

cards.name: Flash KV Accelerator (U.S. Pliops-style NVMe KV engine)
cards.subbranch: LLM inference KV-cache tiering - flash tier with hardware KV engine
cards.what_it_is: A PCIe Gen5 card with an FPGA (AMD Versal / Altera Agilex) key-value engine fronting 8-24 Gen5 TLC NVMe SSDs (Micron 9550, Solidigm, Kioxia). It exposes a KV-block API to vLLM/Dynamo through a NIXL plugin and stores KV on NAND instead of DRAM: a U.S. competitor to Pliops XDP LightningAI.
cards.why_it_could_work: The material swap is NAND for DRAM. Enterprise NVMe at ~$0.30-0.60/GB holds 1M tokens of Llama-70B FP8 KV (164 GB) for ~$0.003/h, so caching pays if reused once per ~78 h, against ~1.35 h for DDR5. One Gen5 SSD reloads a 128k context in ~1.8 s vs ~41 s recompute. NAND stopped rising in Oct 2026, with surplus forecast for 2H27.

cards.name: Compressed CXL Expander (licensed inline compression IP)
cards.what_it_is: An FPGA CXL 2.0 Type-3 card (Altera Agilex 7 R-tile or AMD Versal Premium) that runs licensed inline memory-compression IP (ZeroPoint Technologies, Gothenburg, or an LZ4-class core) in front of 256-512 GB DDR5. It exposes ~2x the physical capacity to Redis/Valkey/Memcached and VM hosts and would later tape out as an ASIC.
cards.why_it_could_work: The IBM MXT lineage and ZeroPoint claim 2-4x on compressible data [UNVERIFIED-T]. At $20-32/GB, a 2x ratio on 512 GB is worth ~$10-16k of DRAM per card in 4Q26. Linux already proves the demand: zswap plus Intel IAA hardware DEFLATE.

cards.subbranch: HBM alternatives at system level: CPU-DRAM-resident MoE inference
cards.what_it_is: A U.S.-integrated 2-socket AMD EPYC 9005 server with 768 GB-1.5 TB of 12-channel DDR5 RDIMM and 1-2 NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 / RTX 5090-class GPUs. It runs KTransformers/SGLang CPU-GPU hybrid inference of open frontier MoE models (Kimi K2.5, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, GLM-5) and is sold with a support and model-update subscription to firms that cannot send data to cloud APIs.
cards.why_it_could_work: Holding ~1 TB of weights in HBM takes ~$240k of H200-class GPUs. In DDR5 it is ~$20k at 4Q26 prices (~$8k in the glut). KTransformers documents Kimi-K2.5 on 2x4090 + >=600 GB RAM and DeepSeek-V4-Flash on one RTX 5090 + >=200 GB RAM. Decode roofline: ~23 tok/s per socket (614 GB/s, 32B active INT4), ~46 tok/s NUMA-aware. Modelled BOM ~$56k (4Q26) / ~$44k (glut), list ~$72k / $56k at 22% hardware GM.

It is exposed as CXL PMEM with Global Persistent Flush and targets database write-ahead logs and storage-array journals that lost their home when Intel killed Optane PMem.

IBM FlashCore Module 5 replaced capacitors with Everspin MRAM for power-loss protection (Oct 2026), so persistent journaling memory has buyers. Sub-microsecond durable commits beat NVMe flush latency by 10-100x.

cards.name: LPDDR 'HBM-lite' Memory Chiplet (UCIe/AIB-attached)
cards.what_it_is: A fabless memory-controller chiplet with a UCIe or open AIB 2.0 die-to-die interface on one side and 4-8 LPDDR5X channels on the other. It would be taped out at GlobalFoundries 12LP+ (Malta, NY) or TSMC N6 and sold or licensed to AI-ASIC startups that cannot get HBM allocation, giving ~0.5-1 TB/s and 128-512 GB per package at LPDDR prices.
cards.why_it_could_work: HBM takes ~22% of DRAM wafer starts for ~9% of bits and ~3x DDR5's wafer area per bit. HBM4 2027 asks of ~$4.5-4.9/Gb (~$36-39/GB) and allocation to the big GPU makers leave smaller ASIC teams short. LPDDR5X proves the bandwidth-per-pin path (NVIDIA Grace), and open AIB RTL lowers die-to-die IP cost.

Samsung HBM-PIM/LPDDR5X-PIM and SK hynix AiM show vendor interest.

cards.name: Memory-Fabric SuperNIC (Ethernet-attached DRAM for GPUs) - acquired away
cards.subbranch: Far memory over RDMA / custom memory-fabric silicon
cards.what_it_is: A custom NIC/switch ASIC that attaches pools of commodity DDR5 (behind CXL controllers) to GPU servers over 800G-3.2T Ethernet/RDMA, giving each GPU tens of TB of 'elastic' memory for KV cache and weights. This is the Enfabrica ACF-S/EMFASYS concept, taped out at TSMC.
cards.why_it_could_work: GPUs need far more memory than HBM supplies (KV for a 128k Llama-70B context is 40 GiB at BF16). Ethernet/RDMA reloads a 128k context in ~0.5 s vs ~41 s recompute, and commodity DDR5 at ~$26/GB beats HBM-in-GPU at ~$180-250/GB.
